In Frame 1, a bright hand and phone at the bottom-right (~3-5 m, outside the camera wearer's arm's reach) sit behind a mid-ground clothing display wall (~1.2-1.8 m) to the left and a dark mirror cavity on the right, while in Frame 2 a bright object enters at the bottom-right corner (~3-5 m) behind the slatted clothing rack on the right (~3-5 m) and the white wall and dark doorway receding to the left (~1.5-2.5 m). Compared to the RGB strip alone, the depth map clearly isolates the receding person and their withdrawn hands and phone from the visually busy patterned garments and plaid shirt in front of them, while also showing the continuous slant of the wall plane from right to left. However, the depth map is unreliable on the mirror in Frame 1 (rendering the reflection as a bright shallow surface rather than a flat surface at ~3-5 m), flattens the hanging garments out of the wall plane in Frames 2-3, and shifts the background wall in Frames 4-5 to near-white due to relative depth normalization when the person and hands move very far away.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map provides 2D silhouettes and class labels for major regions across Frames 2-5, after leaving Frame 1 entirely blank. In Frame 2 it segments the angled central wall (~1.5-2.0 m from the camera wearer, positioned between the unsegmented right clothing rack and left doorway), and in Frames 3 and 4 it tracks a pink 'person' mask exiting toward the right (~3-5 m) from the center (~3-5 m, outside arm's reach), standing directly behind and progressively revealing the right side of the background wall mask (~3-5 m in front of the person).
